title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer hysteresis ordering during regional failover
author: Miguel Santos
release_notes: Fixes a race in SLO enforcer hysteresis ordering that could cause repeated regional failovers and load-shedding thrashing; improves stability during high-pressure failover events.
body: Context: Recent incidents showed the SLO enforcer could enter a thrashing state during cross-region failover when backoff/hysteresis timers were applied out-of-order under concurrent state transitions. This caused repeated load-shedding and unnecessary regional failovers. Motivation: stabilize the failure domain and avoid cascading degradations for customers during transient infra events. Summary of changes: 1) ensure deterministic ordering of hysteresis transitions by introducing a compare-and-advance step guarded by a per-policy monotonic sequence number, 2) add jittered backoff window (configurable backoff_jitter_ms) to reduce synchronized retries across replicas, 3) tighten the enforcer state machine to avoid double-decrement of healthy-node counts during in-flight transitions, 4) add unit and integration tests that reproduce the race pattern observed in production, and 5) improve metrics to surface hysteresis transitions and dropped requests during failover. Testing and validation: added new unit tests (hysteresis_test.go) and an e2e scenario in perf-canary harness that reproduces the race; ran the canary repeatedly and verified no thrashing for >1000 simulated failover cycles. CI: initial run had one flaky integration test related to timing; increased test timeouts and re-ran — all checks passed. Rollout plan: immediate hotfix rollout to Dedicated and Private via canary (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with metric gates on slo_enforcer.hysteresis_transitions_per_min and slo_enforcer.load_shed_rate. Rollback: helm chart values include previous image tag and disable_backoff_jitter flag to revert behavior quickly. Related work: ENG-10234 incident, ENG-10456 follow-up stability task. Notes: this is urgent hotfix aimed at preventing customer-impacting thrash; no API surface changes.
